data.title: Sawan Fasts & Rituals: A Devotee’s Journey
data.author: Guruji

photos.title: Preparing the Vrat Thali
photos.description: Fruits, bel patra, milk, and sweets—each item placed with devotion, offered as a symbol of love and surrender.

photos.title: Tying the Kalava
photos.description: The red sacred thread (kalava) is tied with a prayer — a reminder of protection and divine connection.

photos.title: Journey to the Temple
photos.description: Steps taken barefoot, with chants on the lips and faith in the heart — a journey of devotion.

photos.title: Jal Abhishek
photos.description: Pouring water over the Shivling symbolizes surrender, cleansing, and devotion—an act repeated for centuries.

photos.title: The Sacred Beginning
photos.description: Before sunrise, the day begins with a pure heart and a simple resolve to fast for Lord Shiva.

photos.title: The Fast Ends with Faith
photos.description: The day closes with gratitude and quiet strength. Sawan fasts aren't just rituals—they are a return to the self.

photos.title: The Shiva Katha
photos.description: Listening to or reading the stories of Shiva deepens the spiritual bond — a ritual of the soul as much as the mind.

data.title: Colors of Devotion: Sawan Vibes Around India
data.author: Guruji

photos.title: Kanwar Yatra (Pilgrimage of Faith)
photos.description: Millions of devotees walk barefoot to offer holy water to Shiva—an act of deep penance and devotion during Shravan.

photos.title: Temple Decorations (Monsoon Adorned Mandirs)
photos.description: Temples across India glow with green decorations in Sawan, inviting the monsoon’s freshness into sacred spaces.

photos.title: Green Sarees & Mehendi (Shravan Shringar
photos.description: Green, the color of life and fertility, is worn by women during Sawan as they pray for their family’s well-being and longevity.

photos.title: Rain & Reverence (Nature and God Together)
photos.description: Sawan isn’t just a ritual—it’s a feeling. When the skies open, hearts follow, drenching devotion in the rhythm of rain.

photos.title: Regional Rituals (Different States, One Spirit)
photos.description: From Maharashtra’s Shravan Mondays to Odisha’s Bol Bom chants, every region adds its unique flavor to this devotional season.

photos.title: Sawan Jhulas (Swings in the Monsoon Breeze)
photos.description: In North India, especially in UP and Bihar, swings are hung in gardens during Sawan, symbolizing joy and the playful love of Shiva and Parvati.
